title: [storage] the storage north star "Bytes a landing leaves behind" (the day's gain over its landings, by source) and S1 "Rebuildable bytes on disk" (scratch, build cache, test databases), measured from 180's storage readings
prompt:
Spawn, objective 185 [storage] (after 180; the owner's core metric set of 2026-11-14 18:42, the lead's split of 180): the storage north star, "Bytes a landing leaves behind", and S1, "Rebuildable bytes on disk", measured from the storage readings.

176 shows both as "not measured yet". 180 records once a day what each storage source really holds on disk: a `host.storage_bytes` control record, each source with its bytes or why it is not measured. This objective reads the two figures from those records. S2 ("Kept content against its floor") stays not measured yet; it is 184's.

Base: 180 (n180 o180 8c7d9cce, sync/obj-180), on 176 R2 (744b5311 on 007563ed). R1 was on 180 dc89c348 (old history); moved by content, its +/- lines unchanged.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs: `Figure`, `figure_json`, `NOT_MEASURED_YET`, `adopted`, `lines_at`;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/storage.rs: `storage_line`;
- crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs: `HOST_STORAGE_BYTES` (180); schema.sql's `spawn_events_landing` index.

What changes:
(1) `HOST_STORAGE_BYTES` (host.rs) also reads two more things:
   - `older`: the newest reading recorded at least a day before the newest one;
   - `landings`: how many landings were recorded after `older` and up to the newest, 0 without both readings.
   A landing is either of these, on any mission and source:
   - a `task.landed`, which the integrator writes;
   - an owner's landing: a `source.moved` naming its request. A deploy's `source.moved` names none, and is not counted.
   The landings are read through `spawn_events_landing`, between the two readings' session_seq.
(2) `Figure` gains two fields, given by `figure_json` only when set:
   - `note`: why a figure is not measured, or what it was read from;
   - `by_source`: the figure split by source.
(3) storage_line builds two figures from the readings. `lines_at` sets the readings on the storage report as `readings`.
   - storage.bytes_per_landing, the north star.
     - Value: the sum, over the sources measured in both readings, of newest bytes minus older bytes, divided by the landings (whole bytes).
     - Each source's gain is in `by_source`.
     - The note says "<n> landing(s) in the <h> h between the two readings (the integrator's and the owner's, on every mission and source)". It then names any source measured in one reading only, which is left out of the sum.
     - It has `as_of_ms`, the newest reading's time.
     - It is not measured, with a note, in four cases:
       - with no reading;
       - with one reading: "not measured yet: the figure needs two storage readings a day apart";
       - with no source measured in both;
       - with no landing between the readings. `by_source` is still given then.
   - storage.rebuildable_bytes, S1: the newest reading's scratch + build_cache + test_databases, each in `by_source`. If one of them is not measured, S1 is not measured, and its note gives each one's why.
   Both keys leave `NOT_MEASURED_YET`; only storage.kept_share stays in it.

What stays as it is:
- the readings (180);
- every other figure;
- the ranges file: the two keys take a range as any figure does, and none is proposed here;
- the hourly host.core_lines sample, which carries the two values when they have one.

Polled reads: `HOST_STORAGE_BYTES` runs on every /api/core-lines answer, the hourly sample and the guardrail alerts' readings. It reads three things:
- the newest reading, through its index;
- the newest reading a day older, a walk back through the same index over the daily readings;
- a count over `spawn_events_landing` between two session_seq values: a day or two of landings.
Read-only timing on live (once readings exist; before, it reads nothing):
  psql "$SPAWN_DATABASE_URL" -c "explain analyze with readings as (select e.session_seq as seq, e.recorded_at_ms as at_ms from spawn_events e where e.session_id = 'session_control' and e.event_name = 'control.recorded' and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' ->> 'type' = 'host.storage_bytes'), newest as (select * from readings order by seq desc limit 1), older as (select r.* from readings r, newest n where r.at_ms <= n.at_ms - 86400000 order by r.seq desc limit 1) select count(*) from spawn_events e, newest n, older o where e.session_id = 'session_control' and e.event_name = 'control.recorded' and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' ->> 'type' in ('task.landed', 'source.moved', 'deploy.finished') and e.session_seq > o.seq and e.session_seq <= n.seq"
Expected a few ms; the lead times it.

Tests:
- serve/core_lines/storage.rs:
  - the_storage_north_star_is_the_days_gain_over_its_landings (new);
  - rebuildable_bytes_are_scratch_build_cache_and_test_databases (new);
  - the_storage_line_reads_health_storage (two lines added: the two figures, null without readings).
- serve/core_lines/observability.rs: the_observability_line_gives_unpriced_use_interventions_and_the_count_not_measured. Its storage gains two readings, so the count of figures not measured stays 9.
- crates/spawn-postgres/tests/storage.rs: storage_readings_are_read_back_with_the_landings_between_them (new). It checks:
  - which reading is the older one: a reading less than a day before the newest is not;
  - task.landed and the owner's landing are counted;
  - a deploy's source.moved and deploy.finished are not;
  - landings before the older reading or after the newest are not.

(1) One reading, two days old:
   - the north star is not measured yet, with value null, and its note says why;
   - S1 is the reading's scratch, build cache and test databases (3 MiB), each in `by_source`.
(2) A second reading, an hour old. Between the two: two task.landed, an owner's landing and a deploy's source.moved. Before the older one: a task.landed.
   - The north star is 6 MiB over 3 landings. `by_source` gives scratch 6 MiB, build_cache, transcripts and test_databases 0.
   - Its note names live_database and session_backups as measured in one reading only, and says "3 landing(s) in the 47 h between the two readings".

(3) A newest reading a minute old, its scratch over its bound: S1 is not measured, and its note is "not measured: scratch: over the bound of 1200 s (9 files read)". The north star is still read against the reading two days back, not the one an hour old: "3 landing(s) in the 47 h".
